title: 4-year-old girl with abdominal pain
arrival: A 4-year-old girl is brought in by her mother for mild, intermittent abdominal pain that began this morning.
keyCriterion: High-risk vital sign — heart rate 165 bpm (threshold >160 for ages 1–4 years)
feedbackWhy: This patient does not meet any red or yellow criteria. However, her heart rate is above the high-risk threshold of 160 beats/min for children aged 1–4 years. She should not be moved directly to the low-acuity or waiting area without immediate review by a supervising clinician. The supervising clinician or local protocol should determine her final triage category.
reviewNote: This case's source-defined outcome is “Up-triage / immediate review by a supervising clinician,” distinct from a plain Yellow or Green. Confirm the scoring convention used for this against learner answers of Yellow or Green (currently: Green = under-triage, Yellow/Red = over-triage).

airway_red.text: No stridor. No central cyanosis. No respiratory distress.

circulation_red.text: Peripheral pulse strong. Capillary refill 2 seconds. No bleeding. No cold extremities.

disability_red.text: No convulsions. No altered mental status, stiff neck or fever.

other_red.text: Age 4 years. No trauma, poisoning, threatened limb or surgical diagnosis.

airway_yellow.text: No swelling of the mouth, throat or neck. No wheezing.

circulation_yellow.text: Eating and drinking normally. No vomiting, diarrhoea or dehydration.

disability_yellow.text: Alert and calm. Walking without assistance. Not in severe pain.

other_yellow.text: Abdomen is soft. No malnutrition, trauma, rash or surgical diagnosis.

exampleShows: No red or yellow criterion is met.
Her heart rate of 165 is above the 160 high-risk threshold for ages 1–4 years, so she needs immediate review by a supervising clinician. The clinician or local protocol decides her final category.
